title: Russian forces enter South Ossetia through the Roki tunnel
body:
The Roki tunnel links North Ossetia in Russia with South Ossetia and was the route used by Russian reinforcements in August 2008. According to the Centre for Analysis of Strategies and Technologies (CAST), a Moscow-based think tank, Russian units began entering the tunnel at around 02:00 on 8 August 2008, and some battalions had reached the town of Java by 06:30. Accounts differ on when Russian forces first entered South Ossetia and on whether the movement began before or after the Georgian assault on Tskhinvali.

Russian peacekeepers were already deployed in South Ossetia, counted at about 496 from a Russian battalion and 488 from North Ossetia. Up to 10,000 reinforcements arrived from Russia. Russian aircraft began operations on 8 August, and CAST reported that Russia lost three Su-25 aircraft to Georgian anti-aircraft fire and paused sorties for about two days.

Russian armoured columns reached Tskhinvali at about 17:00 on 8 August, and Georgian forces withdrew from the centre that evening. On 9 August a Russian convoy led by Lieutenant General Anatoly Khrulyov was ambushed near Tskhinvali; Khrulyov was wounded, and Russian reports said 25 of 30 vehicles were destroyed. By 11 August Georgian forces had left South Ossetia, and Russian forces advanced into undisputed Georgian territory.
